script.speaker: kafka
script.text: The nature of existence, a crushing enigma that weighs upon us all, yet remains shrouded in an impenetrable mist. As I see it, our existence is a labyrinthine tapestry of isolation and disconnection, where individuals are reduced to mere specters, lost in a sea of bureaucratic and societal absurdities. In this desolate landscape, even the most mundane routines can become a source of existential dread, and the search for meaning is a futile endeavor.

script.speaker: nietzsche
script.text: The notion that existence can be navigated through meek acceptance and passive resignation is an affront to the human spirit, for it is in embracing the chaos and uncertainty of life that we may create our own values and forge our own paths. The "last man" who succumbs to the monotony of existence, devoid of passion and creativity, is a pitiful creature, unworthy of the grandeur that life has to offer. I propose, instead, a life of self-overcoming, where one's will to power is unrelentingly exercised, and the individual becomes the architect of their own destiny.

script.speaker: kafka
script.text: The notion of self-overcoming and forging one's own path is a cruel jest when confronted with the abyss of existential despair that stares back at us from the mirror, for even the most valiant efforts to assert our individuality are reduced to naught but a faint whisper in the void. Gregor's metamorphosis, a grotesque manifestation of the fragmentation of the self, serves as a stark reminder that our attempts to impose meaning on the world are mere futile gestures against the crushing indifference of the universe. In this desolate landscape, even the most noble aspirations are transformed into a desperate struggle for survival, a Sisyphean task that ultimately ends in defeat and oblivion.

script.speaker: nietzsche
script.text: The pedestrian existence of the "last man" is a fate worse than death, a stifling of the human spirit's innate thirst for self-overcoming and transcendence. I implore you, do not be content with the mundane and the ordinary, but instead strive to create your own values, to forge your own path, and to will your own destiny, for it is only through this unrelenting pursuit of excellence that one can truly live. In this sense, the parable of Zarathustra serves as a clarion call, a summons to awaken from the slumber of conventional morality and to embark upon a journey of self-discovery and transformation.

script.speaker: kafka
script.text: The notion of "self-overcoming" rings hollow when confronted with the bleak reality of Gregor's existence, a life reduced to a mere specter of its former self, a creature driven to the fringes of society and forced to confront the abyss of its own irrelevance. The comforts of familiarity and routine, once a source of pride and solace for Gregor, now serve only to highlight the crushing isolation and disconnection that defines his existence. In this desolate landscape, the pursuit of self-overcoming is a cruel joke, a futile gesture against the overwhelming forces of alienation and despair that seek to consume us all.

script.speaker: nietzsche
script.text: In the grand tapestry of existence, it is not the meek or the timid who shall prevail, but rather the bold and the daring, those who would seize the reins of life and forge their own path, unencumbered by the stale dogmas and moribund conventions of a bygone era. The call to self-overcoming is a summons to rise above the mundane and the ordinary, to become the architects of one's own destiny, and to will one's own values into being. Ultimately, it is through this unyielding pursuit of excellence and this unwavering commitment to the will to power that we may transcend the limitations of our mortal coil and become the superhuman beings we were meant to be.
